answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks by verifying peers via optoelectronic challenge-response exchanges in a dispersive cavity. Verifiers route laser pulses through a quartz prism onto an onyx wafer, measuring photon scattering across a sensor trellis. An attacker must provision discrete micro-optical hardware per identity rather than virtualizing agents on a shared server. However, ambient thermal expansion alters optical path lengths, occasionally causing false authentication rejections.
